I remain committed to passing the Women's Health Protection Act and protecting reproductive freedom nationwide.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133927384/629550176/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4M2EyYmE5NC1lNjZmLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dPYJO36d4hrMKYKIJ9VwgJH7Z34THSJovykH3oDjuXA=&emci=fde0e732-356f-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=83a2ba94-e66f-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ceid=14565883)

| | Four years ago this week, the Supreme Court issued its decision in the _Dobbs_ case, overturning _Roe v. Wade_ and stripping away the right that generations of women had relied on. I remember the shock, anger, and heartbreak that many of us felt in that moment. But what's happened since then has been even more devastating. Politicians in states like ours rushed to enact bans, criminalize care, and interfere in deeply personal medical decisions that should belong to patients, their families, and their doctors. Texas now has some of the most extreme restrictions in the nation. **We are seeing women forced to travel hundreds of miles for basic care, delay critical medical treatment, and navigate impossible medical crises during their most vulnerable moments.** Unfortunately, _Dobbs_ was never the end goal. It was just the beginning. The same politicians who promised they only wanted to return abortion policy to the states have continued pushing for restrictions nationwide. They have targeted medication abortion, threatened access to contraception, attacked IVF, and opened the door to government intrusion into private healthcare decisions that should never be subject to political control. That's why I continue to support the Women's Health Protection Act. Your rights shouldn't depend on your ZIP code. No one should be forced to leave their community or travel hundreds of miles just to receive healthcare. **The Women's Health Protection Act would restore the protections of _Roe v. Wad_ e and secure a nationwide right to abortion care, keeping politicians out of the exam room permanently.** But my commitment to reproductive freedom does not stop there. I have also supported legislation to protect access to contraception, safeguard IVF and other assisted reproductive technologies, defend the right to travel across state lines for reproductive healthcare, and ensure patients have access to accurate information about their healthcare options. This is a fundamental matter of personal freedom — the freedom to make your own healthcare decisions, to do what is best for your family, and to be trusted with your own life without fear of legal repercussions. **As long as attacks on reproductive freedom continue, I will fight for legislation that protects bodily autonomy, restores reproductive rights, and ensures every person can make their own healthcare decisions with dignity, privacy, and autonomy.** Fundamental rights should not disappear because of who sits on the Supreme Court or which state someone happens to call home. Four years after _Dobbs_ , the core question remains: Who should make these decisions — women and their doctors, or politicians? I know where I stand. Four years ago today, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade.
I remember exactly how I felt: Heartbroken. Shocked. But Determined.
I knew what was coming next: The politicians who spent decades promising that Roe was "settled law" immediately began rushing to ban abortion, criminalize healthcare decisions, and strip away rights that generations of women had fought to secure.
And unfortunately, those fears became reality.
As a scientist, I believe healthcare decisions should be guided by evidence, medicine, and the relationship between a patient and their doctor.
As a mother, I believe my daughter deserves the same rights and freedoms that previous generations fought for.
And as a legislator, I've fought back every step of the way.
But four years after Dobbs, the truth is simple: This fight is not over. Not even close. The same politicians who celebrated the end of Roe are now pushing for more restrictions, more government intrusion, and more attacks on reproductive healthcare.
That's why this election matters. It's why control of Congress matters. And it's why I'm running.
Now more than ever, we need leaders who will protect reproductive freedom, defend evidence-based healthcare, and trust women to make their own decisions. So today, on this difficult anniversary, I'm asking you to help us continue that fight. Can you chip in any amount to send a pro-choice fighter to Congress? subject: 4 years ago today, SCOTUS decided to kill women
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY DEFEND OUR COURTS, NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE
body:
While the exact number of women who have died as a result of this decision is difficult to calculate, each year brings new heartwrenching stories, and more unacceptable deaths.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001K4YCN1uN-ALCZI-cX3VbUjiSNLAe__13rmlme-4nwZvJqr0jqgqtkrfZzkflHzrYHJetodNJ3wI5OgcmuAGT4i-QfARay0xVKArI5SQ13RXtX-3qPN1Aw1v-dYSGwo_9N6fNynnZgcSTZHy1hG8HiOVOIYB4vB8pFCdxowckzCftTndO3o9yZXYYSCStPVBIwG92T1r7W_Yuu92B68GK4S7G6aTFn92nydgUhX2lyp8=&c=-_TpI11xhzxQ6qT39QAKafJ-AlN-MwzhzzJuI2Bs5bBbJ9JhppeNQA==&ch=iVN6F5WgwAYyWY6G_TW5MS6az2FUIrrI_MglSCMqp4F45FT5oMmvdg==)
---
|
Peter,
Today marks the 4 year anniversary of the Dobbs decision--the Supreme Court ruling that overturned Roe v. Wade and opened a Pandora's box of extreme ban abortion across the country.
The consequences of that decision have been fatal.
The bans have turned routine care into a death sentence for many women in red states. Doctors, afraid of breaking the law, are holding back basic treatment from women suffering miscarriages and pregnancy complications. So women who could have been saved are dying preventable deaths because they didn't get the care they needed in time.
While the exact number of women who have died as a result of this decision is difficult to calculate, each year brings new heartwrenching stories, and unacceptable deaths.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001K4YCN1uN-ALCZI-cX3VbUjiSNLAe__13rmlme-4nwZvJqr0jqgqtkrfZzkflHzrYHJetodNJ3wI5OgcmuAGT4i-QfARay0xVKArI5SQ13RXtX-3qPN1Aw1v-dYSGwo_9N6fNynnZgcSTZHy1hG8HiOVOIYB4vB8pFCdxowckzCftTndO3o9yZXYYSCStPVBIwG92T1r7W_Yuu92B68GK4UPBBl_qry9QxijoCpbBHqo=&c=-_TpI11xhzxQ6qT39QAKafJ-AlN-MwzhzzJuI2Bs5bBbJ9JhppeNQA==&ch=iVN6F5WgwAYyWY6G_TW5MS6az2FUIrrI_MglSCMqp4F45FT5oMmvdg==)
---
It's worth remembering exactly how we got here. During his first term, Donald Trump put three justices on the Supreme Court. One by one, they sat before the Senate and looked the American people in the eye. One by one, they called Roe v. Wade settled law.
Maine's MAGA Senator Susan Collins infamously cast the deciding vote for Brett Kavanaugh, then told the country he'd given her his personal word that Roe was safe. But in 2022, Trump's MAGA justices showed us what those words were worth. They overturned Roe, ripped away a half-century of protection, and unleashed a wave of cruelty and death on women across the country.
But Dobbs is not the end of the story. It can be undone -- and Defend Our Courts is fighting to do exactly that.
The Constitution never set the number of justices. Expanding the court takes no amendment, just an act of Congress, which has changed the court's size 7 times already. To reclaim the court it just requires Democrats to reclaim the White House, the Senate, and the House.
And just as much, it requires the political will to expand the court. That's what Defend Our Courts is spearheading. We're building the political momentum for Supreme Court reform, so that when Democrats retake power, we can reverse the death and suffering that the Dobbs decision has caused.
[On this 4th anniversary of the Dobbs decision, we can fight back and reverse this fatal decision. Can we count on you to make a contribution of $50, $25, or whatever you can spare to help us unpack the court?](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001K4YCN1uN-ALCZI-cX3VbUjiSNLAe__13rmlme-4nwZvJqr0jqgqtkrfZzkflHzrYpHUe97yInfaFfjTVtHTBV2ruG9KBcMC-QfXW2QcxzzTJj4oJHH93yhIm0LsgOo7S5yPXybM3_QRnru3WqAwa2iiWDrPKqSiHWFEw--fuL4RKha_g_-_s29juaHxKtx7-pPY7C7h-iZs4lVWA7t29NCWJMuDzlSE7CfD2D3YiciPYyPp7GVQSCQ==&c=-_TpI11xhzxQ6qT39QAKafJ-AlN-MwzhzzJuI2Bs5bBbJ9JhppeNQA==&ch=iVN6F5WgwAYyWY6G_TW5MS6az2FUIrrI_MglSCMqp4F45FT5oMmvdg==)

clean_body: While the exact number of women who have died as a result of this decision is difficult to calculate, each year brings new heartwrenching stories, and more unacceptable deaths. | | | | | == | Peter, Today marks the 4 year anniversary of the Dobbs decision--the Supreme Court ruling that overturned Roe v. Wade and opened a Pandora's box of extreme ban abortion across the country. The consequences of that decision have been fatal. The bans have turned routine care into a death sentence for many women in red states. Doctors, afraid of breaking the law, are holding back basic treatment from women suffering miscarriages and pregnancy complications. So women who could have been saved are dying preventable deaths because they didn't get the care they needed in time. While the exact number of women who have died as a result of this decision is difficult to calculate, each year brings new heartwrenching stories, and unacceptable deaths. | == It's worth remembering exactly how we got here. During his first term, Donald Trump put three justices on the Supreme Court. One by one, they sat before the Senate and looked the American people in the eye. One by one, they called Roe v. Wade settled law. Maine's MAGA Senator Susan Collins infamously cast the deciding vote for Brett Kavanaugh, then told the country he'd given her his personal word that Roe was safe. But in 2022, Trump's MAGA justices showed us what those words were worth. They overturned Roe, ripped away a half-century of protection, and unleashed a wave of cruelty and death on women across the country. But Dobbs is not the end of the story. It can be undone -- and Defend Our Courts is fighting to do exactly that. The Constitution never set the number of justices. Expanding the court takes no amendment, just an act of Congress, which has changed the court's size 7 times already. To reclaim the court it just requires Democrats to reclaim the White House, the Senate, and the House. And just as much, it requires the political will to expand the court. That's what Defend Our Courts is spearheading. We're building the political momentum for Supreme Court reform, so that when Democrats retake power, we can reverse the death and suffering that the Dobbs decision has caused. == | | | == | == | == | | | == | == | == | | | | == | In solidarity, Defend our Courts | | | | | | | | | | == | | | | | == | | | | Mail checks to: | | | | Defend Our CourtsP.O. subject: Why JD Vance’s story meant so much to Charlie Kirk
body:
A story of faith lost, tested, and found again

| | | |
---
| | | Fellow Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: A story of faith lost, tested, and found again | | | | | | | Fellow Patriot, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. Now's the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both. And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further -- and touch more young lives -- than ever before. For Charlie, The Turning Point USA Team P.S. Fellow Patriot, many young people leave home with a foundation of faith, only to have the culture chip away at it, piece by piece. JD Vance knows what that struggle looks like. Today marks four years since Trump’s handpicked Supreme Court justices overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , stripping away nearly 50 years of constitutional protections for reproductive rights and unleashing a wave of Republican attacks on reproductive freedoms across the country. Right now, 20 states ban or severely restrict abortion access beyond what existed under the standard set by _Roe v. Wade_. In 13 of those states, there is a total ban, including civil and criminal penalties for health care providers. **These attacks didn’t start in Congress. [ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Can I tell you a secret?

Some of the most important work that the government does will never make
the news, but as Secretary of State, it’s some of the work I’m most proud
of. Because I know firsthand the government works best when it’s there
when you need it, and gets out of the way when you don’t.

That’s why I’ve worked from day one to make life easier for all
Michiganders. Together, we:

* Cut average wait times to 20 minutes or less. Michigan’s motor vehicle
department went from having some of the longest wait times in the
country to a model of efficiency.
* Created over 150 self-service stations at branch offices and grocery
stores. Michiganders could renew license plates and driver’s licenses
while picking up the week’s groceries.
* Reduced the need for Secretary of State office visits. We doubled the
number of services available online, and now 60% of transactions are
completed without an office visit.
* Brought our elections from 34th to 2nd in the nation. Michigan’s
elections are now among the most secure and accessible in the country.

It’s not the flashiest work, but it’s the kind of policies that
hardworking Michiganders notice. When you’re not having to wait hours in
line to take your driving exam, or when you can renew your car’s tags
while picking up dinner, you feel the impact of good governing.

I’m running for governor because I believe the government can and should
make life easier for all Michigan families. As governor, I’ll use every
single tool available to expand rural healthcare, build more housing, and
make life less expensive for hardworking families.

But, I can’t do it without the help of supporters like you. Michigan is
one of the most competitive states in the entire country, and our MAGA
opponent has the backing of big billionaires and the DeVos family. I can
only win this race with your support, so today, I’m asking: [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/6954?t=1001&akid=1695%2E181023%2EKLF3gt ]Will you
make your first

body:
Free Nibbles!

| | | [ ](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn11JJNENg30eeUPXVkqayxCfDLIkkjdPcC_U3XuHRoCIwMELeQenzQ2oHmoOYJU340&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=happy_hour_invite&n=1)
---
Dear Peter,
---
Will you be in (or near) Corpus Christ this week? Please join us for a **FREE** (no door cover) Convention Happy Hour this Friday at 4pm. We'll have free appetizers and sweets to share! [**RSVP HERE**](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/convention_happy_hour?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=happy_hour_invite&n=2 "RSVP HERE")
---
---
Thank you again for supporting our campaign. Just a reminder: Running for Congress was never something I planned, but I am deeply frustrated by the current state of our country—the constant attacks on our democracy and institutions, and our reckless approach to war. I love my work as a kindergarten (and soon-to-be first grade) teacher and I am a farm girl at heart, but I—no, **WE can no longer sit on the sidelines**. This moment demands leadership, especially in districts like ours. That’s why I am running for Congress against Republican incumbent Michael Cloud—one of Trump's very most loyal congressmen— in Texas’s 27th District. **I am committed to flipping this district blue. With your help, I know we can do it.** When elected, I will work tirelessly to ensure that:
* **Healthcare is a universal right** , not a privilege, and people have guaranteed access to abortion and full reproductive rights.
* **Every job pays a living wage** , and families benefit from universal daycare.
* **Public education is fully funded** , and all children have access to early education.
* **Agricultural policy incentivizes conservation** , dramatically reduces taxpayer costs, and requires big agribusiness to pay the farmers' real price for raw goods.

For the past two decades, I have served my community in a variety of roles: as a member of the school district’s bond oversight board, a 4-H club manager, a Meals on Wheels volunteer, a founding member of the Lockhart FFA Booster Club, president of the Lockhart Athletic Booster Club, and on numerous other committees dedicated to serving our community. Through these experiences, I have learned that relationships matter most—and that we all want the same basic things: to live in dignity, security, and peace, surrounded by love and care.

Her campaign priorities include lowering costs for families, protecting public education, strengthening democracy, expanding rural healthcare, supporting reproductive rights, protecting farmers, and championing economic investments for working Texans.

These facilities are designed to break people and make them voluntarily withdraw their lawful asylum claims before they are seen by an immigration judge. The Whatcom County Council, in a 5-2 vote, said that the county will not aid this system of destroying families. Thank you Council Members Rienstra, Scanlon, Galloway, Buchanan, and Boyle. But the fight continues. This moratorium does not apply to any City limits within the county. We don't want to see any more facilities joining the existing ICE processing center within the Ferndale City limits. Join the Bellingham Trouble Makers who are continuing to lead the resistance against detention centers. Reminder: Join us tomorrow in Ferndale at Fringe Brewing to meet Tomas and the campaign staff! Valdez!

Claire is a union organizer, New York state assemblymember, democratic
socialist, and now, the next Justice Democrat to represent NYC in
Congress!

She and fellow primary winner Darializa Avila Chevalier in neighboring
NY-13 will be the first joint UAW and DSA members elected to the House,
bringing the promise of uniting the labor movement and organized left
together to deliver for working people.

Despite facing nearly $1 million in outside Super PAC spending for her
opponent, Antonio Reynoso, Claire won this heated race with a clear vision
rooted in labor organizing, economic justice, and opposition to war and
genocide.

Justice Democrats proudly became the first national progressive group to
support her candidacy less than a week after she launched her campaign.

Unlike her opponents, Claire didn’t come to politics through party
machines or electoral ambition, but by working low-wage customer service
jobs and eventually finding her power in her union, UAW Local 2110.

She launched with a bold platform of Workers Deserve it All: Unions for
All, Medicare for All, and Housing for All — paid for by taxing the
wealthy and corporations that have rigged the economy.

Claire was an early and outspoken opponent of Israel’s assault on Gaza,
becoming one of the first elected officials in New York State to call it a
genocide and demand a ceasefire. She has vowed not to vote for another
dollar in U.S. funding for Israeli apartheid, has organized elected
officials to defend the right to protest, and participated in civil
disobedience against U.S. government complicity.

From the beginning, Claire has had the moral clarity and political courage
the Democratic base is rightfully demanding from its elected officials.
While she didn’t take a dime of corporate PAC money, her main opponent
accepted donations from AIPAC and real estate investors.

Reynoso also received nearly $1 million from super PACs in the final weeks
of the race, most of which came from pop-up Super PACs with undisclosed
donors or affiliations. But it wasn’t enough to stop Claire and her
organized, people-powered campaign!

This victory was another monumental defeat of AIPAC donors, the real
estate lobby, and a liberal NYC establishment waning in influence with the
ascension of an organized Democratic Socialist movement locally that
Justice Democrats has consistently been aligned with.

Before the New York primaries, we were already going to gain more seats in
Congress this year than over our last two cycles combined. Now, with our
victories in NY-13 and NY-07, this is officially Justice Democrats’ most
successful cycle to date — and that’s only because of people like you!

Friend...

Could a simple ritual before bed be the answer to burning, swelling, and tingling feet — including those pins and needles on the bottoms of your feet?

The National Library of Medicine says, “YES!”

Your feet have a natural recovery cycle that's supposed to kick in every night — calming irritated nerves and easing the swelling.

But after 50, that nightly recovery cycle slows down. So instead of waking up to calmer feet, you wake up to the same burning and tingling… or worse.

Here's the good news: you can give that nightly “foot reset” a jump-start — right from your recliner.

Reset your feet tonight: –>
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MTd9AAwAAAAAAV7TAG64f27yGqkGB_gwZXKmwjvjLP7K0PKk34sQTpm-C76a6Nc3aRG5fT9MZVbXC3NOpjdbV6e1n-ulhEzyu5js5KpUjVmNn-BMkmM
The simple at-home ritual that calms burning, swelling, and tingling feet

This is getting a lot of attention right now…

Because for years, people were told the only options were creams, compression socks, or pills that mask the pain temporarily…

So eventually the burning, tingling, and discomfort comes right back.

The good news is you can reset your feet tonight.

I think this is the closest thing yet to an answer for tired, aching feet:

name: Voto Latino
subject: 6.7 million Latinas were impacted by the Dobbs decision
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
The impact of the Dobbs decision is still harming millions today.
#
Peter,
After 4 years, the Supreme Court’s decision to overturn _Roe v. Wade_ continues to harm millions of people across the nation — impeding abortion access, disrupting economic futures, and putting health and lives at risk.
**Women of color bear the heaviest burden of this crisis, facing the highest systemic and economic barriers to care.** _For the Latina community, the impact of the Dobbs ruling is uniquely devastating, Peter._
From low insurance coverage to anti-immigrant discrimination, Latinas face a wall of compounding obstacles to basic healthcare, and these bans have only made those disparities worse. Here’s a breakdown of just how much this decision has impacted our community:
* Nearly 6.7 million Latinas — 43% of all Latinas of reproductive age — live in the 26 states that have banned or are likely to ban abortion.

* More than 3 million Latinas living in these restrictive states are economically insecure. Those denied abortion care are significantly more likely to be pushed deeper into poverty.

* Nearly half of all Latinas in these 26 states are already mothers. When mothers are denied care, the economic security and development of their existing children are directly threatened.

* Over 1 million impacted Latinas report not speaking English well or at all, creating substantial hurdles to finding culturally competent care.

The only way to stop these attacks is to change who holds power.**We must elect people who are actually going to fight for reproductive rights at the state level and in Washington.**
**[Will you chip in $3 right now to help Voto Latino register voters and build the political power needed to defend our reproductive freedom?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260624-1.gTEwFK&amount=3&refcode=em20260624-294&t=1&akid=294%2E1366028%2EJKwWW2)**

Thank you,
Voto Latino

subject: Why JD Vance’s story meant so much to Charlie Kirk
body:
| | | |
---
| | | Peter,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: | | | | | | | Peter, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. Now's the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both. And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further -- and touch more young lives -- than ever before. For Charlie, The Turning Point USA Team P.S. Peter, many young people leave home with a foundation of faith, only to have the culture chip away at it, piece by piece. JD Vance knows what that struggle looks like. So do countless young Americans who Turning Point USA is reaching right now. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044 |

Four years ago today, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade .
The Trump-appointed conservative majority took away a woman’s right to choose—something that had been cemented in law for almost 50 years—and left it up to the states whether someone could determine her own health and future.
Now, thirteen states have near-total abortion bans.
While working as a sexual assault prosecutor, I saw firsthand how important it is for women to have access to choice. These bans have done nothing to bring justice to them, to help families, or to protect Americans. In fact, just a year after SCOTUS overturned Roe , we saw a nearly 10% jump in the maternal mortality rate here in the U.S.
When I am elected to Congress, I will do everything in my power to restore our equal rights to medical care— because that is what abortion care is.
If you agree, please support our campaign. In Congress, I will fight for our reproductive rights, and I will fight to invest in women’s healthcare more generally so that our families can have better outcomes. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cbh_email-26q2?refcode=x_260624_Dobbs_act]

Friend, Fourteen years ago, DACA changed the lives of hundreds of thousands of young people by giving them the chance to work, study, and build their lives in America. Today, that promise is under attack. According to a recent report, Dreamers are losing their jobs while waiting months for DACA renewals that used to take only weeks to process. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133934153/629574052/900375698?refcode=em-6.24.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzM1MWEzNWUtZjI2Zi1mMTExLWFjOWMtMDAwZDNhNTRiZWQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WovBOpUH64XFwrAsccT5AA13p5u_v1xsefuf0vdAFjc=&emci=3151a35e-f26f-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=3351a35e-f26f-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ceid=27336212) As the son of Vietnamese refugees, I know how much the promise of America means to immigrant families. My family opened a corner market where I worked every day after school. DACA gave Dreamers that same chance. The stories coming out of immigrant communities are heartbreaking. People who followed every rule are suddenly losing jobs, losing income, and living in fear because renewal applications are sitting in bureaucratic limbo. At the same time, the Trump Administration has wrongfully deported more than 150 DACA recipients and continues to target immigrant families who have built their lives here. That is wrong – these are our neighbors, coworkers, students, and small business owners. They contribute to our communities every day and deserve certainty about their future. **[That's why I'm asking you to stand with me: Will you add your name to demand permanent protections for DACA recipients and an end to these harmful delays?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133934154/629574053/900375698?refcode=em-6.24.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzM1MWEzNWUtZjI2Zi1mMTExLWFjOWMtMDAwZDNhNTRiZWQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WovBOpUH64XFwrAsccT5AA13p5u_v1xsefuf0vdAFjc=&emci=3151a35e-f26f-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=3351a35e-f26f-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ceid=27336212)**

# [Trump's Bessent just dropped a jaw-dropping 3% GDP boom forecast for this year](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent voiced confidence Wednesday that[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/3db4ce07-7af6-4bc2-b0a6-799492ee8608?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[the U.S. economy will achieve 3% growth before year-end](https://substack.com/redirect/3db4ce07-7af6-4bc2-b0a6-799492ee8608?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the Iran conflict winds down, despite recent sluggish quarters.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Strong Underlying Economy Persists** : Bessent highlighted robust fundamentals and noted the economy ran near 4% growth in February before the strikes.
* **Three Three Three Plan Intact** : The administration still targets 3% growth, 3% deficit-to-GDP and 3 million barrels daily oil output increase.
* **Recent Growth Lagged Sharply** : GDP expanded 1.6% in Q1 after just 0.5% in Q4 2025, following full-year 2.1% advance.
* **Deficit Progress Visible Already** : The shortfall stands 9% lower year-over-year at $1.25 trillion through eight months of fiscal 2026.

# [Hormuz nightmare ends, oil prices plunge below $70 in minutes](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
U.S. crude futures **[slid below $70 a barrel Wednesday as tankers resumed transit](https://substack.com/redirect/fad88587-696d-491c-bc43-32dba9304a2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/fad88587-696d-491c-bc43-32dba9304a2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)through the Strait of Hormuz, easing supply fears, while President Trump directed the DOJ to probe alleged gasoline price gouging.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **WTI Hits Session Low** : West Texas Intermediate touched $69.63, last trading down 4% at $70.22 after falling below $70 for the first time since March.
* **Brent Crude Falls Further** : International benchmark declined 4.2% to $73.83, reaching its lowest level before the February U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran.
* **Trump Demands Pump Relief** : The president posted on Truth Social accusing big oil firms of gouging and ordered immediate DOJ investigation.
* **Maritime Evacuation Advances** : Over 11,000 seafarers will begin exiting via Hormuz under safety guarantees coordinated by the IMO with Iran, Oman and the U.S.

# [OpenAI just unveiled its super secret Jalapeño AI chip with Broadcom](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OpenAI and Broadcom on Wednesday[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/b3cb2543-8346-4560-9322-6877142c513a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[introduced their first custom silicon chip named Jalapeño](https://substack.com/redirect/b3cb2543-8346-4560-9322-6877142c513a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for AI inference, designed end-to-end in nine months as the ChatGPT maker pushes to control its full compute stack.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Inference Focused Processor** : The new Intelligence Processor targets serving models to users in ChatGPT and will be manufactured by Broadcom.
* **Deployment Timeline Set** : Initial rollout planned by end of 2026 with small prototypes late this year, scaling heavily through 2027 and 2028.
* **Demand Called Insatiable** : OpenAI President Greg Brockman and Broadcom CEO Hock Tan described customer compute needs as exceeding supply for years ahead.
* **Stack Building Strategy** : Move follows OpenAI deals with AWS Trainium, AMD and Cerebras to diversify beyond Nvidia GPUs amid explosive growth.

# [Congress to force Big Tech to pay for massive AI grid costs](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The House Energy and Commerce subpanel begins debate Wednesday on the Ratepayer Protection Act, requiring data center operators such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft **[to cover power grid upgrades amid voter frustration over rising utility bills.](https://substack.com/redirect/dfa08f82-817e-4c1d-a3c3-206402607232?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
* **Large Load Standard Mandated** : Utilities must evaluate rules making big customers pay for new generation, transmission and grid upgrades they trigger.
* **Bipartisan Sponsorship Confirmed** : Reps. Gabe Evans of Colorado and Kathy Castor of Florida introduced the measure codifying White House pledge elements.
* **Tech Giants Signed Pledge** : Major builders including Meta and xAI have agreed in principle to fund new electricity production for AI facilities.
* **Midterm Election Context** : Legislation arrives months before voters decide control of Congress with widespread complaints about data center electricity costs.

# [Treasury to oversee released Iranian frozen assets](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f05f8a-16ac-4b54-8339-88dd7ce80aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Qatar Oversight Planned** : Initial releases will occur under Treasury officials in Doha to recycle money back into U.S. foodstuffs and medicines.
* **Iranian Rejection Noted** : Tehran officials rejected U.S. dictation on spending, insisting purchases would follow price and quality criteria alone.
* **Escrow Account Structure** : Funds placed in U.S.-controlled accounts with enforcement through banks, sanctions and sanctions pressure.
* **Domestic Benefit Highlighted** : Arrangement positions released money to benefit U.S. farmers, food producers and pharma companies.

body:
This past Saturday, I had the chance to speak at a reception during the Washington State Democrats Convention.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260624-6389-footer&t=1&akid=6389%2E420207%2ElLvFBZ)
Peter,
This past Saturday, I had the chance to speak at a reception during the Washington State Democrats Convention in Spokane, I made the case for where our movement—and our party—needs to go next:
**It’s not enough for us to just show up for the last six weeks of an election. We have to stay engaged and organize all year, every year, everywhere, and every day to fight for what’s right.**
The Trump administration is attacking our freedoms, tearing families apart, gutting public institutions, and rigging the economy for billionaires while working people struggle to afford healthcare, groceries, and rent.
Our job as Democrats is not only to fight back against that agenda. It is to offer a better one—to build a country where everyone can afford to live with dignity and opportunity.
And that’s exactly what I’ve been doing.
My Medicare for All PAC will spend more than _$2 million_ this cycle, putting money behind strong progressive candidates across the country so they can stand up to the dark money and AIPAC dollars lined up against them.
And it works.
It worked when we helped elect Analilia Mejia in New Jersey. It worked when we pushed Daniel Biss to victory in Illinois. It worked for Randy Villegas in his primary in California. And we are going to keep getting each of these people across the finish line in November.
**And when we’re in the majority, we won’t just be playing defense.** We’ll be able to fight forward for a country that works for all of us — with a vision not defined by Donald Trump, but by the world we want to live in. For example:
* **My Ultra-Millionaire Tax** would make the wealthiest finally pay their fair share and fund childcare, housing, and healthcare for the rest of us.
* **The Congressional Progressive Caucus’s Affordability Agenda** tackles the cost-of-living crisis head-on.
* **My Monopoly Busters Caucus** is taking on the corporate giants jacking up your prices.
* And of course, **Medicare for All**.

Every piece of this work sets the stage for 2028. We swept in 2025: Virginia, New Jersey, Georgia, and Zohran Mamdani's history-making win in New York. That's not an accident, it's what happens when we fight for working people. And the momentum hasn't stopped — we've overperformed in special election after special election.
But in order to keep this momentum going and ensure we’ll finally have the power to check this president, I need your help. I don’t take a dime from corporate PACs, and I don’t have billionaires on speed dial to cut a check at a moment’s notice. I’m counting on grassroots supporters like you to power everything we’re doing right now.
[**So if you can, please pitch in $3, or any amount that works for you, so that we can take back the House and finally govern in a way that restores our democracy and delivers for working people.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260624-1.x2GrAu&refcode=em20260624-6389&amount=3&t=2&akid=6389%2E420207%2ElLvFBZ)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260624-1.x2GrAu&amount=3&refcode=em20260624-6389&t=21&akid=6389%2E420207%2ElLvFBZ)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260624-6389-footer&t=22&refcode2=6389_420207_lLvFBZ&akid=6389%2E420207%2ElLvFBZ)**

But in order to keep this momentum going and ensure we’ll finally have the power to check this president, I need your help. I don’t take a dime from corporate PACs, and I don’t have billionaires on speed dial to cut a check at a moment’s notice. I’m counting on grassroots supporters like you to power everything we’re doing right now. In solidarity, Pramila Jayapal | | Email us: info@pramilaforcongress.com

Peter, today is the four-year anniversary of the Dobbs decision, and this day is a reminder of how quickly the rights we rely on can be taken away.

I think about the moms and daughters I know who now face more uncertainty when they go to the doctor. I hear from people who are scared about losing coverage or being forced to travel long distances for care. That fear shows up at kitchen tables and in doctor’s offices. It is not abstract. It is daily life.

As mayor I saw how fragile access can be when decisions are made far from our communities. I want a Congress that listens to families, protects care, and protects women’s fundamental right to control their own bodies.

We can make a difference by passing commonsense protections for reproductive care and making sure everyone here has the right to choose what is best for their family. But it will take a campaign that can meet this moment and keep fighting every step of the way.

If you can, would you consider chipping in to help us protect care and defend personal freedoms? Either way, thank you for reading, standing with me, and for everything you do to keep our communities strong.

With gratitude,
Paige Cognetti

name: Dr. Maxine Dexter
subject: Abortion access is healthcare.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Maxine for Congress
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q2?refcode=x_260624_Dobbs_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q2?refcode=x_260624_Dobbs_act]
Peter,
I am a mother. I am also a critical care physician. I very clearly understand how hard being pregnant is on a woman when things go as planned—let alone when things go tragically wrong. So believe me when I say, abortion is healthcare .
Right now, reproductive rights are under attack. Four years ago today, Trump’s handpicked Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade , undoing almost 50 years of precedent and opening the floodgates to dangerous, near-total abortion bans across the country.
Restricting abortion access has put lives at risk and threatened the healthcare millions of women rely on. It’s created a culture of silence and shame while endangering the lives of pregnant women. In the last four years, we’ve seen higher maternal mortality and young girls trapped into being a mom before they are ready.
I’ve cared for patients facing some of the most difficult times of their lives. I have helped families navigate through tragedies and medical emergencies. I know how infuriating it is when politicians interfere in decisions that should be made by patients and their families, in consultation with their doctors.
Too many families have already been affected by this, but we can ensure that future generations have more rights and freedoms than their grandparents, not fewer.
In order to do that, we need to take back the House and Senate—which means we need your support. Will you stand with us in this fight? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q2?refcode=x_260624_Dobbs_act]

name: Gretchen Whitmer
subject: What I mean when I say I’m “Fighting Like Hell”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fight Like Hell PAC
body:
I’m doing everything in my power to ensure that my daughters have the same rights I’ve had my entire life |
#
---
Folks, it’s been four years since the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_. Now, more than one in five women live in a state with an abortion ban. When I say I’m “Fighting Like Hell,” I’m talking about fighting for my daughters and young people like them. I’m doing everything in my power to ensure they have the same rights I’ve had my entire life. **And thanks to this movement, we’ve protected and expanded care so Michiganders can access the resources they need.** But Republicans are trying to ban abortion nationwide, and we need to make sure that they don’t win at the ballot box and make their agenda a reality. We need to come together and elect leaders up and down the ballot who fight like hell for our rights. **[I need you with us. Friends, the Trump administration is attacking California’s efforts to improve air quality and protect public health, again .
They’re doubling down and attempting to block our longstanding authority to address air pollution and climate change and enforce stringent clean vehicle standards that protect our state and residents.
It is wrong, and it is illegal. So we’re fighting back: We filed a lawsuit against Trump’s EPA defending our ability to address air pollution and enforce emission standards that protect our state.
To keep this fight going, please chip in today: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
CONTRIBUTE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
For half a century, administrations from both parties have respected California’s authority to improve our air quality and enforce our own standards through EPA Clean Air Act waivers. But now, the EPA's unlawful attempt to reclassify these waivers as “rules” allegedly subject to Congressional disapproval would illegally restrict our ability to use these important tools.
This would mean more pollution, poorer air quality, more climate change, more market uncertainty, and greater health risks for communities already overburdened by emissions.
California will continue to fight back against the Trump administration’s illegal attacks and lawless overreach to protect our communities and environment.
If you’re with me on this, I’m asking for your help to power our work. I’m up for re-election this year, and I can’t win without your support. Will you chip in today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Healthcare costs are too high.
Most politicians respond by promising new programs, new spending, or more bureaucracy.
I have a different plan.
Here's how we'll bring down healthcare costs in Ohio immediately in 2027:
1\. [Prosecute Medicaid fraudsters – aggressively.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._z1sQ) Every dollar stolen by fraudsters is a dollar taken from hardworking taxpayers.
2\. [Strike a deal with the federal government](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.) that allows Ohio to keep a majority of the savings. If Ohio helps root out waste, Ohio taxpayers should benefit.
3\. [Put billions of dollars back in the pockets of law-abiding Ohioans.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.) Instead of rewarding fraud and waste, we'll return those savings to the people who earned them.
[It's a simple idea: stop subsidizing fraud and start rewarding honest citizens.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
[If you agree, I'd be honored to have your endorsement:](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-1Rg)

name: Marlena, Team AnderBois
subject: A day on Team Sue
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
body:
| |
---
Hi! I'm Marlena, and I just joined Sue’s campaign as an intern! The team was kind enough to let me borrow her email for a minute to say hello, tell you what it’s like to work for Sue, and why I’m doing it. I'm a Brown alum (Go Bruno!), and after spending the last year teaching in Spain, I was looking for a way to get involved back in Rhode Island. Then I got the chance to come on the team to help with research and data.
---
---
One thing I've learned already is that there’s a LOT more going on on campaigns than shaking hands and giving speeches. There is data to compile and volunteers to organize, events to prepare for, phone calls to make, doors to knock, supporters to connect with, and a million little details that help keep everything moving. If you've ever wondered what campaign life looks like, I thought I'd give you a quick peek into a typical day for me:
---
| |
* 8:00 AM — Coffee and emails.

* 8:30 AM — Catch up on campaign news, community updates, and what's happening around the state.

* 10:00 AM — Review new volunteer signups and track campaign activity across Rhode Island.

* 11:00 AM — Check in with the team and help with research projects.

* 12:30 PM — Lunch break 🍔

* 1:15 PM — Update volunteer records and help keep our supporter database organized.

* 3:00 PM — More research, data projects, and helping the team prepare for upcoming events.

* 5:00 PM — Wrap up and get ready to do it all again tomorrow! 🌞

---
**Every day looks a little different, but no matter what each one holds, there’s something Sue always keeps at the center of the campaign: This is about the people.** **_And that’s why I chose to work for Sue._** We can’t make Rhode Island a better, cleaner, safer, more equitable place to call home if we don’t keep YOU at the heart of everything we do. And every volunteer signup, every event attendee, every supporter who takes a few minutes to read an email like this helps move that collective mission forward. I hope you’re as excited as I am about electing Sue for Lt. Gov so we can show just what the office can do. The team asked me to make sure you were following her on social media too, so I’m sending along these links in case you need them:
---
|
🦋 BlueSky:
**[https://bsky.app/profile/sueanderbois.bsky.social](https://sue4ri.com/l/BGUIcCYujLrF)**

🗣️ Facebook:
**[https://www.facebook.com/SueAnderBois](https://sue4ri.com/l/NuR3ku9eBQCu)**

📷 Instagram:
**[https://www.instagram.com/sueanderboisri/](https://sue4ri.com/l/bmhUXQ7chvzv)**

---
Thank you for being here! Onward! —Marlena
---
---

body:
Three progressive challengers took on the establishment in Congressional primaries and won big
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2307%2E791427%2EOx_-IO)
Friend — **last night was huge!**
Three progressive challengers took on the establishment in Congressional primaries and won big, pushed along by incredible grassroots energy and on-the-ground community organizing.
Brad Lander ran on denouncing AIPAC and Israel’s genocide, and promised voters that he would fight for an end to the violence and occupation.
Claire Valdez made it clear that she would put renters and workers first, not wealthy landlords and corporate CEOs.
Darializa Avila Chevalier spoke to the affordability crisis and pledged to fund healthcare and childcare rather than bombs and wars overseas.
Friend — when I was first elected to Congress, they called us ‘The Squad.’ Four progressive women of color who were ready to reject the status quo and fight for the better future we know is possible.
**Now, because of the tireless work of this movement, The Squad is bigger than ever before, and growing fast.**
These victories make it clear that the American people are quickly waking up to the realities of our time. The wealthy and powerful are taking home more and more while the rest of us are left to struggle to afford the essentials. Trump has exposed the deep corruption, authoritarianism, and militarism of the far-right, and voters of all kinds are ready for something drastically different.
But remember, election season is far from over, and we are now less than two months from primary day here in Minnesota. I need your help if we’re going to hold this seat and continue to lead the opposition to Trump, ICE, AIPAC, and the rest of MAGA.
[**Help me join this exciting new class of progressive fighters in Congress by chipping in to my campaign today. We are building something real across this country, a movement that rejects business as usual and dares to dream of a bold way forward. I need you with me in this fight. Friend — when I was first elected to Congress, they called us ‘The Squad.’ Four progressive women of color who were ready to reject the status quo and fight for the better future we know is possible. Now, because of the tireless work of this movement, The Squad is bigger than ever before, and growing fast. These victories make it clear that the American people are quickly waking up to the realities of our time. The wealthy and powerful are taking home more and more while the rest of us are left to struggle to afford the essentials. Trump has exposed the deep corruption, authoritarianism, and militarism of the far-right, and voters of all kinds are ready for something drastically different. When I was first elected last year, **I said that I believe small states can do big things** — and there is no limit to what we can accomplish when we work together to make people’s lives better. That holds true now more than ever.

I’m going to keep going every single day between now and November, and I’m going to need your help along the way.

name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
subject: Trump put American lives on the line.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
From the moment Donald Trump launched his unauthorized war with Iran, I opposed it.
I opposed it because the Constitution does not give one president the power to drag our country into a war whenever he feels like it.
I opposed it because there was no clear strategy, no defined endgame, and no honest explanation of what American families were being asked to sacrifice.
And most importantly, I opposed it because American service members would be the ones placed in harm’s way.
American troops were put in danger.
Billions of taxpayer dollars were poured into another conflict in the Middle East.
And while all of that money was disappearing overseas, families here at home were paying the price every time they pulled into a gas station.
That is not strength. It is reckless, wasteful, and unconstitutional.
I voted for the War Powers Resolution because the power to take this country to war belongs to Congress and the American people, not one unaccountable president.
Now, after months of bloodshed, rising prices, and enormous military spending, the administration is pointing to a tentative agreement and asking us to forget how we got here.
I will not forget.
Equal Opportunity Now was built to support leaders who will stand up when presidents abuse their power, who will protect working families from the cost of reckless decisions, and who understand that patriotism means telling the truth before disaster strikes, not declaring victory after the damage is done.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 today to help Equal Opportunity Now elect leaders who will oppose reckless wars, defend our Constitution, and put American working families first? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE NOW >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
We warned them from the beginning. Now we have to make sure this never happens again.
-- Raja Krishnamoorthi

This is about more than simply defending our democracy, even if we could snap our fingers and return to what we had in 2016. This is about truly reforming our democracy to live up to the promise of our country, where every person matters and every vote gets to count equally .

Those recent Supreme Court decisions include curtailing abortion rights by overturning Roe v. Wade and the ruling in Louisiana v. Callais that significantly weakened a key section of the Voting Rights Act.
After so much damage, we simply can't return to politics as "normal". Too many lines have been crossed, too many people harmed, too many rights have been lost. We're fighting for a people-focused revival of our democracy. One that serves the public interest and us as citizens, not the right and powerful.

When Governor Ned Lamont and Fairfield's state representatives celebrated a 75% state reimbursement for the Dwight Elementary School rebuild, it was good news for Fairfield taxpayers. No one should begrudge Fairfield's students a safe, modern school. Dwight has had longstanding concerns involving air quality, aging infrastructure, early childhood education, and special education space.
But the announcement should raise an obvious question in Greenwich:

[Pledge your support](https://substack..iWeS4qFHCIfMaYpWA5UYvNYQDk80Qb5mqfexE9w5iUM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=203443006)
_**Why does Fairfield receive a 75% reimbursement while Greenwich 's Central Middle School rebuild receives only 20%?**_
The contrast is striking.
According to [Greenwich Time](https://substack.com/redirect/cf0425be-6f97-47df-9c98-373082834052?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Greenwich's Central Middle School project is expected to cost roughly $112 million. The town had initially expected only a 6.9% reimbursement, or about $7.7 million, before Greenwich's state delegation secured a 20% rate, bringing the expected reimbursement to about $22 million.
That was presented as a win, and compared to 6.9%, it was.
**But now compare that to Fairfield.**
According to [CT Insider](https://substack.com/redirect/b20a137e-23bc-4424-ace5-c22506511d8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Fairfield's Dwight Elementary School rebuild is projected to cost roughly $76 million, and the state has agreed to reimburse 75% of the project. Fairfield's state representatives also announced that this amounts to roughly $57 million in state aid.
_**Put another way, Fairfield 's school project costs far less than Greenwich's, yet Fairfield is receiving more than twice the state dollars.**_
For Greenwich taxpayers, that means the town is still expected to carry roughly 80% of the Central Middle School burden. For Fairfield taxpayers, the state is expected to carry roughly 25% of the Dwight burden.
_**That is not a small difference. That is a completely different deal.**_
This comes as House Representatives Steve Meskers and Hector Arzeno have also touted an additional $8 million boost for the Old Greenwich School renovation. The [Greenwich Democratic Town Committee](https://substack.com/redirect/5da74fb7-0ab3-40cf-a9ee-ab4218ffeeec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) stated that Arzeno and Meskers secured an additional 15% reimbursement rate tied to the inclusion of pre-K classrooms, unlocking more than $8 million in additional state funding. [Greenwich Free Press](https://substack.com/redirect/068d6bf1-8af3-4e5d-a592-0f6fb3e1aefc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) also reported that the change came after an amendment allowed the Old Greenwich School project to qualify despite a prior technicality tied to the project's application date.
**That money matters. Any additional reimbursement that reduces pressure on Greenwich taxpayers is welcome.**
But the bigger issue remains: _**if Hartford can find special flexibility, special language, and enhanced reimbursement for some projects, then Greenwich should not be expected to celebrate partial relief while other towns receive far more generous deals.**_
The demographic comparison makes the question even more important. Greenwich and Fairfield are similar-sized Fairfield County communities. According to U.S. Census QuickFacts, [Greenwich](https://substack.com/redirect/d6397589-5c42-47a5-b919-a8f0ed2120ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has an estimated 2025 population of 64,801, while [Fairfield](https://substack.com/redirect/0932a7df-3394-488b-a616-8c8e810d75d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has an estimated 2025 population of 66,262. Both are high-performing, high-cost, highly educated towns with strong public school systems and substantial property tax burdens.
Yes, Greenwich has a higher median household income: about $206,130 compared to Fairfield's roughly $172,432. Greenwich also has a far higher median owner-occupied home value, about $1.7 million compared to Fairfield's roughly $780,500.
But that does not tell the whole story.
_**Greenwich is far more diverse and economically diverse than many in Hartford seem willing to admit. It is not just home to hedge funds and billionaires.**_
According to U.S. Census QuickFacts:
* Greenwich has a higher poverty rate than Fairfield: 6.1% compared to 4.7%.
* Greenwich has a higher foreign-born population: 22.5% compared to 12.6%.
* Greenwich has a higher Hispanic population: 14.4% compared to 6.7%.
* Greenwich has more households where a language other than English is spoken at home: 25.1% compared to 16.0%.

Greenwich has seniors, renters, working families, small business owners, municipal employees, young families, immigrants, first-generation Americans, and taxpayers who are being asked to absorb enormous local capital costs.
In other words, the assumption that "Greenwich can just pay for it" is lazy public policy, and it is time for Hartford to know that.
Connecticut's school construction reimbursement formula is supposed to take municipal wealth into account. The [Connecticut Department of Administrative Services](https://substack.com/redirect/770a073e-6647-4e17-b2b7-80a7c8221747?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) explains that reimbursement rates are calculated annually using a statutory formula that starts with the adjusted equalized net grand list per capita, known as AENGLC, as a measure of municipal wealth. The same state page also explains that there are special reimbursement opportunities for projects that meet certain statutory criteria, including early childhood programming.
That is exactly the point.
_**When Hartford can create special outcomes, waivers, incentives, and enhanced reimbursement rates, Greenwich has every right to demand transparency and fairness.**_
*This is not about taking anything away from Fairfield. Fairfield's representatives did their job. They fought for their town. They made the case that Dwight Elementary needed state support, and they delivered a major win for their taxpayers.
The question is whether Greenwich's taxpayers are getting the same level of urgency from Hartford.
Greenwich sends a tremendous amount of tax revenue to the State of Connecticut. Greenwich helps fund the state budget, state programs, state borrowing, and state aid that flows to other communities. Yet when Greenwich needs help replacing aging school buildings, it is too often treated as if it should simply be grateful for whatever it gets back.
That is not fairness. That is not accountability. That is not a serious way to govern.
The Central Middle School rebuild is not a luxury project. Old Greenwich School is not a luxury project. These are major public infrastructure projects for students, teachers, families, and the community. Like Fairfield's Dwight project, they involve health, safety, educational adequacy, long-term planning, and taxpayer impact.
If Fairfield can receive a 75% reimbursement for a school rebuild, Greenwich should not be told that 20% is the best Hartford can do.
Connecticut needs a clearer, fairer, and more transparent school construction reimbursement system. Special reimbursement rates should not appear to depend on political influence, committee assignments, budget negotiations, or who has the most leverage in Hartford. If early childhood education, special education programming, air quality, safety, and modernization justify enhanced reimbursement in one town, then the same standards should be available to every town that meets them.
Greenwich taxpayers deserve more than polite thank-yous and partial relief. They deserve representatives who will fight for every dollar, demand equal treatment, and make sure Hartford remembers that Greenwich is part of Connecticut too.
Fairfield fought and won a 75% reimbursement.
Greenwich should not be stuck footing the bill.
Greenwich deserves its fair share.
_**Jonathan Goldstein is running to represent Greenwich 's 150th District. Greenwich deserves more than announcements and press releases. Greenwich deserves a representative who will fight for our fair share, demand equal treatment, and stop allowing Hartford to treat our taxpayers as a blank check. His website is[ www.goldsteinforct.com](https://substack.com/redirect/6e5e012b-b818-4748-8fdc-357ad55e2f93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_

Greenwich helps fund the state budget, state programs, state borrowing, and state aid that flows to other communities. Yet when Greenwich needs help replacing aging school buildings, it is too often treated as if it should simply be grateful for whatever it gets back. That is not fairness. That is not accountability. That is not a serious way to govern. The Central Middle School rebuild is not a luxury project. Old Greenwich School is not a luxury project. These are major public infrastructure projects for students, teachers, families, and the community. Like Fairfield's Dwight project, they involve health, safety, educational adequacy, long-term planning, and taxpayer impact. If Fairfield can receive a 75% reimbursement for a school rebuild, Greenwich should not be told that 20% is the best Hartford can do. Connecticut needs a clearer, fairer, and more transparent school construction reimbursement system. Special reimbursement rates should not appear to depend on political influence, committee assignments, budget negotiations, or who has the most leverage in Hartford. If early childhood education, special education programming, air quality, safety, and modernization justify enhanced reimbursement in one town, then the same standards should be available to every town that meets them. Greenwich taxpayers deserve more than polite thank-yous and partial relief. They deserve representatives who will fight for every dollar, demand equal treatment, and make sure Hartford remembers that Greenwich is part of Connecticut too. Fairfield fought and won a 75% reimbursement. Greenwich should not be stuck footing the bill. Greenwich deserves its fair share. Jonathan Goldstein is running to represent Greenwich 's 150th District. Greenwich deserves more than announcements and press releases. Greenwich deserves a representative who will fight for our fair share, demand equal treatment, and stop allowing Hartford to treat our taxpayers as a blank check.
