He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Are you still paying 20% (or more) interest on your credit cards? Change can happen in a generation. **I know because it happened to me.**
Let me explain:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133954117/629624813/1482048376?refcode=email_062426_immigrant-heritage-month&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMmRjM2EzOS0xYzcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zVUowvbdOSa0iJNJcDbwy_UzgNlT0XvwiNJgoYhjer0=)
When my dad was five years old, he immigrated from Mexico to the United States.
He picked cotton and tomatoes in the fields of the Rio Grande Valley, all the while dreaming that one day he would work his way out of poverty and make it to the middle class.
My parents taught me the value of hard work. And I grew up believing that if we worked hard, anything was possible.
But when I got to college, I realized my parents didn’t have the money to pay for my tuition and their groceries. So I worked all kinds of odd jobs to put myself through school. It took seven years, but I finished my degree and became the first person in my family to graduate from college.
When my daughter was born, I felt in my core the same determination that drove my parents: **there was nothing that would keep me from doing everything in my power to shape a stronger, more equitable future for Amelia and her generation.**
But right now, Washington is being run by Donald Trump and his MAGA majority, who are, quite frankly, willing to purposefully tank our economy if it means their party can get ahead.
They have pushed reckless tariffs, skyrocketed gas and grocery prices, passed a damaging budget bill that ripped away healthcare from tens of thousands of Oregonians, and launched _countless_ attacks on our immigrant communities.
Families are doing _everything_ right, but are still struggling to get by. We deserve better.
**Today, I am fighting with the same grit and perseverance that drove my parents, and that continues to drive me. **

Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
LAST CALL: Sign the pledge to support a brighter future for working Texans
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Hear%20America.png]
These last few weeks, TOP has teamed up with our friends at the Organizing Revival Network to promote the Willing to Fight Pledge [https://toptx.us/orn] -- a commitment to a vision and future where ALL Texans have the ability to grow and thrive.
We're only a few days from our end-of-June deadline. Can you sign the pledge today to help us reach our completed pledge goal? [https://toptx.us/orn]
It only takes a minute and your feedback provides our groups with a look at what issues matter most to you and your family.
👉🏾 Take the pledge now! [https://toptx.us/orn]
Celebrating our communities and building fellowship this Juneteenth
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/01%202026%20Juneteenth.jpg]
TOP staff and members celebrated Juneteenth alongside community partners at events across Houston, Dallas, and San Antonio this past week. Through that celebration we honor the ancestors we stand on the shoulders of, and recommit to working tirelessly toward a future where race and class are no longer barriers to justice and opportunity in our country.
Juneteenth serves as a renewed call to unite against racial and economic injustice, so that we can chart a path toward a stronger Texas and nation that uplifts and empowers every Black person, regardless of their background or economic status. This is why we organize. This is why we are stronger together.
Taking time this summer to refuel for the second half of 2026
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/TOP%20summer%202026%20out.jpg]
TOP offices will be closed Saturday, June 27 - Sunday, July 5, as we take time to rest, rejuvenate, and prepare for a busy rest of 2026 filled with organizing and getting out the vote! You can still keep in touch with us online, though. Give us a follow on the following platforms:

Instagram [https://www.instagram.com/texasorganizingproject]

Estamos a pocos días de nuestra fecha límite de finales de junio. ¿Podrías firmar el compromiso hoy mismo para ayudarnos a alcanzar nuestra meta? [https://toptx.us/orn]
Solo te llevará un minuto, y tu opinión nos permitirá saber qué temas son los más importantes para ti y tu familia.
👉🏾 ¡Firma el compromiso ahora! [https://toptx.us/orn]

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/01%202026%20Juneteenth.jpg]
La semana pasada, el personal y los miembros de TOP celebraron Juneteenth junto a aliados comunitarios en eventos realizados en Houston, Dallas y San Antonio. A través de esta celebración, honramos a los ancestros sobre cuyos hombros nos apoyamos y reafirmamos nuestro compromiso de trabajar incansablemente por un futuro en el que la raza y la clase social ya no sean barreras para la justicia y las oportunidades en nuestro país.
Juneteenth representa un llamado renovado a unirnos contra la injusticia racial y económica, para así trazar el camino hacia un Texas y una nación más fuertes que impulsen y empoderen a cada persona afrodescendiente, independientemente de sus antecedentes o situación económica. Por esto nos organizamos. Por esto somos más fuertes unidos.
Dedicar tiempo este verano a recargar energías para la segunda mitad de 2026
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/TOP%20Spanish%20summer%202026%20out.jpg]

name: Alex Vindman
subject: Don Jr. attacked me. Again.
body:
I am living rent-free in Don Jr.’s head.
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1113?t=1&akid=780%2E3892029%2EmQcyM4)

Peter —
In a new message to supporters, Donald Trump’s conspiracy theorist son said it makes him **_“nauseous”_** thinking of me in the U.S. Senate.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q22026?refcode=em260624-2&refcode2=780_3892029_mQcyM4&akid=780%2E3892029%2EmQcyM4)
_“A**‘Senator Vindman’ – even writing it makes me nauseous** – would mean nothing but more sinister attempts to undermine and **sabotage everything** Republicans have been working toward. Losing any race stings, but this one would be a **TOTAL DISASTER.** ”_
I take up a lot of space in Don Jr.’s brain, because this follows a long pattern of his attacks against me.
After I testified in front of Congress about his father’s illegal phone call, Don Jr. ran to Fox News and threw a tantrum. It got so bad that even Fox News had to fact check him for lying about me. _Yes, really._
Look, I served 21 years in the Army. I’ve dealt with my share of so-called “tough guys” like Don Jr., so I’m not afraid of them.
But here is what I _am_ afraid of: Donald Trump’s Super PAC has been stockpiling a war chest of $350 million. As polls continue to show a path to victory for us in Florida, some of that money will almost certainly go towards pummeling us in attacks.
**That matters, because in an election as close as ours, it could mean the difference between winning and losing the entire Senate majority.**
The greatest source of donations to help us fight back are emails like this one. So with less than a week until our biggest FEC deadline yet, I am asking:
[**Can you please donate $3 to my campaign for U.S. Senate? Florida is an expensive state for a campaign, and the only way we’ll win back the Senate majority and organize Democrats everywhere is together.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q22026?refcode=em260624-2&amount=3&refcode2=780_3892029_mQcyM4&akid=780%2E3892029%2EmQcyM4)

We'll get right to the point. Last night, Cait Conley officially became the Democratic nominee for NY-17. Today, Mike Lawler is already attacking us. [**We’re respectfully asking you to donate $10 to help us fight back against these attacks and begin the general election on a strong foot.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcyKWf40KHRXV9g3KYxAlX2BXnPLyCycOEYkHBIYk09UAO4t4z2_msg2dv9pBW1iluA17SAHPlaAJkzTFxnx41TQ9UlSDuvb4qygM9cdYezWowvs5jR-Lz7OHBs6FowYLld_BJZeC9rUx3DwKKVsFW1mcF6Qk2y-_zJTM769WmVtdTBysro_DSnGnigemqPPXTbKd82B7suJmai_3vqhhP38RuBwYl_D9K6E1_a5jooKuLlhs6mRb7sFbYyo76UIeP5o5zz0kgdb-NSklImaMdQs_WnKXwWq4Vv7jpjRIise6Y/4rr/TyPtgUFaSJeNSNwRgeqwGw/h0/h001.6fXghva6geKVuD4-sR_FWNxX80VGVF6cVKWPdd65LjI) | [DONATE »](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcyKWf40KHRXV9g3KYxAlX2BXnPLyCycOEYkHBIYk09UAO4t4z2_msg2dv9pBW1iluAFhhi8YmY3SJMXFSKJIshO7hg6SoIhP2HpzXENP3NPF0ZcRH8BitpCUmv60rxuwsTH52mAOVLpC0UFABYqaYUP-gRZjm5nBa9fcAEBmq04O36V2hRMyNfvKCY7iIzjw9SI_VxsrK_PnNRahMeMdIwKOVU_sgxCgnYBTj8EmbDdoeOfyxY4Jrat3s1EauXtEBQ1hg5dHmWl6RWdVry5iUyetPSEZgHuHcjtfYBCaDu8FE/4rr/TyPtgUFaSJeNSNwRgeqwGw/h1/h001.zb7wY9Efdt2HMwEIzSd4_G0hvQdBRPb4UpQjpU7s9Kc)

Mike Lawler is scared. That’s why his MAGA allies spent over $1.5 million in the final weeks of our primary, trying to stop Cait.
Independent polling shows Cait beating Lawler. But these attacks – and the amount of dark money already being spent in this district – are exactly what we talk about when we say this is going to be an uphill battle.
This is one of just three districts nationwide that split their ticket in 2024 for Kamala Harris and a Republican member of Congress.
That means that the GOP is going to spend a virtually unlimited amount of money trying to hold onto this seat.

We _cannot_ wake up on the morning of November 4th, the day after the election, wishing we had done more to protect Jon Ossoff’s Senate seat.
That’s why we are reaching out requesting your support before our June fundraising deadline: [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ossoff-em-jun26**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-jun26.Bh0QdH&refcode=em260624-2-f&utm_campaign=em260624-2-f&t=2&akid=2430%2E5691347%2EEXNvCL)

name: Fran Hong
subject: If we tax the rich . . .
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
New policy inside!
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260624-2956)
Peter,
Wisconsin deserves safe roads, beautiful libraries, and community parks. We need better options for reliable transit and emergency services we can count on when it matters most.
But too many of our cities, towns, villages, and counties are struggling just to afford the basics.
There’s a reason — and a solution.
Rich people and corporations don't pay their fair share. And for decades, the state has underfunded local governments while limiting their ability to raise the revenue they need. That leaves communities with two bad options: go back to voters for referendum after referendum, or cut the services people count on.
My **CITIES, TOWNS & TRANSIT** policy is a roadmap for rebuilding the state-local partnership and giving communities the tools, funding, and flexibility to meet people’s needs.
And that starts with taxing the rich so we can lower property taxes for working families and invest in the services Wisconsin communities depend on.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/14484?t=1&akid=2956%2E105371%2Ez1aBv8)
**Here’s how we’ll do it:**
✅ **Get politics out of local funding** by fixing revenue sharing, increasing local control, and building local funding options
✅ **Tax the rich** so we can lower property taxes for working families and close loopholes for billionaires and corporations
✅**Build transit that works everywhere** — from reliable city transit and smart development to rural transit options, transportation access to healthcare, and expanded Amtrak passenger rail
Get ready for Regional Transit Authorities, rural and suburban microtransit pilots, better intercity bus service, expanded paratransit, safer sidewalks and bike infrastructure, EV charging. And best of all, Milwaukee-to-Madison Amtrak connection!!!!
Because whether you live in Milwaukee, Madison, Minocqua, Menomonie, or Mindoro, you deserve a state government that helps your community get the job done.
[**Read the full plan here.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/14484?t=2&akid=2956%2E105371%2Ez1aBv8)
Wisconsin deserves a government that works for working people, not one that forces local communities to fight over scraps while billionaires and big corporations get away with paying less than they owe.
But building that kind of government means building the kind of campaign that can win — and that takes resources.
[**We have a goal of raising $100,000 before midnight on June 30. It’s the most important deadline of the year. This is the moment that matters.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260624.-5FOLE&refcode=em20260624-2956&t=3&akid=2956%2E105371%2Ez1aBv8)
[**Can you chip in $10, or whatever you can today to help us share this vision with voters across Wisconsin?**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260624.-5FOLE&refcode=em20260624-2956&t=4&akid=2956%2E105371%2Ez1aBv8)
Together, we can tax the rich, lower costs for working families, and build a state where every community has what it needs to thrive.
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260624.-5FOLE&amount=10&refcode=em20260624-2956&t=7&akid=2956%2E105371%2Ez1aBv8)**
With gratitude,
\- Fran
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260624-2956&t=8&refcode2=2956_105371_z1aBv8&akid=2956%2E105371%2Ez1aBv8)**

Four years
have passed since the Supreme Court’s Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health
Organization decision overturned Roe v. Wade and stripped away the federal
constitutional right for abortion.

The fallout hasn’t stopped — it’s accelerated.

In the years since, state legislatures have rushed to enact sweeping
abortion restrictions and total bans, leaving millions of people without
access to care in their own states.

Patients and providers are being pushed into impossible and often
life-threatening situations — delayed treatment, denied care, and
preventable harm that no one should ever have to face.

But the impact of Dobbs goes beyond state law.

The courts have now become the central battleground. Trump and the GOP
have been installing loyalist, anti-abortion judges across the federal
judiciary — lifetime appointments built to outlast any one administration.

These judges don’t need new legislation to reshape access to abortion.
Through incremental rulings, procedural decisions, and narrow legal
interpretations, they can erode existing protections and restrict
reproductive freedom over time.

That’s the quiet danger now: not a single sweeping reversal, but a slow
dismantling from the bench.

That’s where Demand Justice PAC comes in. We’re working to block Trump’s
crony judicial nominees from lifetime appointments and fight for a
judiciary that protects fundamental freedoms. But we need sustained
grassroots support to keep up this work.

court takeover and protect what remains of reproductive freedom in the
courts?

We can’t treat this moment like history. The impacts of Dobbs are still
unfolding — and the courts will shape what comes next.

Thanks for being in this fight,

Demand Justice PAC

subject: 🌶️ do you like green chile salsa? 🌶️
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/1102?refcode=jtk946-fr-ndem-header&t=1&akid=10536%2E400544%2EldPiZD)
---
Hi friend, it's Deb Haaland. This month, we made history by winning all 33 counties in New Mexico and **officially securing the Democratic nomination for Governor**. I couldn't be more proud of the work we've accomplished, or more ready for the fight ahead.
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/10451?refcode=jtk946-fr-nd&t=2&akid=10536%2E400544%2EldPiZD)
---
This moment wouldn't be possible without the strong women who raised me and the values they passed down: work hard, care for your community, and always make room for others at the table. Growing up, I watched my grandmother bake bread in her mud oven and stir huge pots of posole. She taught me that food brings people together, and cooking became one of my favorite ways to connect with family, culture, and community.

One of my _favorite_ New Mexican staples to make is green chile salsa. The taste of fresh tomatoes and local green chile always brings me back home — to my family, our traditions, and the values that shaped me.

I love this recipe so much, in fact, it inspired me to start my very own salsa company to support my family. From finding capital to get started, to overseeing the work in the commercial kitchen, to delivering jars of salsa to mom and pop shops in Los Lunas, Belen, Bernalillo, and more — I was a part of every step, knowing I was supporting my child, contributing to our local economy, and bringing Pueblo culture into grocery stores across the state.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/10451?refcode=jtk946-fr-nd&t=3&akid=10536%2E400544%2EldPiZD)
Food brings communities and people together, friend. When we share a home-cooked meal or baked goods, we share our traditions, our stories, and the care and time it takes to nourish our families. During this campaign, I've traveled across the state, meeting New Mexican families from all walks of life, breaking bread, and sharing my vision for New Mexico.

I've shared my own struggles and listened to theirs. Together, we’ve made exciting plans for the future of New Mexico. I know New Mexicans want a Governor who will fight for affordable healthcare, expand child care, make our communities safer, strengthen our schools, and protect our environment.
**That’s the kind of Governor I will be.**
**I am ready on day one to get to work and deliver progress for our communities, including making it easier for local neighborhood markets to open and for grocery stores to carry home-grown food, especially to eliminate food deserts across New Mexico.**
[**_Pl_** _**ease, if you believe in my vision for a brighter New Mexico, chip in $5 or whatever you can spare now to help me become the next Governor. When you click this link and donate, I'll share my own green chile salsa recipe with you! >>**_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/10452?refcode=jtk946-fr-nd&t=4&akid=10536%2E400544%2EldPiZD)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/10451?refcode=jtk946-fr-nd&t=5&akid=10536%2E400544%2EldPiZD)

Deb

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133956058/629630821/150430950?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTMyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZWM2NzNlZC0yMzcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Yu1n4Z4qUUi1v_iKelxkhZgHI0L3nhHBbZpdv48wsOg=&emci=2e4e52d7-e56f-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=8ec673ed-2370-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ceid=7731215)
---

| | This week, Congress passed the biggest housing bill in 30 years, and **it includes something I've been fighting for since 2022: the first-ever federal limits on hedge funds and private equity firms buying up single-family homes in our communities.** _But now, Donald Trump announced that he canceled the signing of the bill unless and until Republicans pass his voter-suppression act._ For years, working families trying to buy a home have been forced to compete against Wall Street. Hedge funds swoop in with all-cash, no-inspection offers and outbid regular buyers before they ever have a chance. The result? Families get priced out of neighborhoods they grew up in. Homes that should be places to raise a family become profit centers for investors who will never set foot in them. When I first introduced legislation to crack down on this in 2022, Congress had never taken on private equity's grip on the housing market. Not once. The idea that we could actually put limits on how many homes these firms could buy felt like a long shot. **We got it done, and now Trump is holding it hostage.** The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act puts real boundaries on institutional investors purchasing single-family homes. It passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. It's sitting on the President's desk, and he's refusing to sign it until Congress passes Trump’s voter suppression bill. **We’re not going to let this get buried.** Democrats will continue fighting to make housing more affordable. clean_body: Congress passed the biggest housing bill in 30 years, and it includes something I've been fighting for since 2022. | | | | This week, Congress passed the biggest housing bill in 30 years, and it includes something I've been fighting for since 2022: the first-ever federal limits on hedge funds and private equity firms buying up single-family homes in our communities. But now, Donald Trump announced that he canceled the signing of the bill unless and until Republicans pass his voter-suppression act. For years, working families trying to buy a home have been forced to compete against Wall Street. Hedge funds swoop in with all-cash, no-inspection offers and outbid regular buyers before they ever have a chance. The result? Families get priced out of neighborhoods they grew up in. Homes that should be places to raise a family become profit centers for investors who will never set foot in them. When I first introduced legislation to crack down on this in 2022, Congress had never taken on private equity's grip on the housing market. Not once. The idea that we could actually put limits on how many homes these firms could buy felt like a long shot. We got it done, and now Trump is holding it hostage. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act puts real boundaries on institutional investors purchasing single-family homes. It passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. It's sitting on the President's desk, and he's refusing to sign it until Congress passes Trump’s voter suppression bill. We’re not going to let this get buried. Democrats will continue fighting to make housing more affordable. Onward! name: Ellen R. Malcolm, EMILYs List
subject: What we feared is coming true
body:
Think of the damage Republicans can do with two *more* years |
---
It's time to fight. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133956166/629631191/-1282862128?sourceid=1059250&refcode=WUEFER64_20260624_DobbsKicker_ALL&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYzllNWVhMC0yNDcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8FFKIQz3A4UoZloer3TINCDsDaOA9oNIKJy8QzKHkGU=) Peter, when _Roe v. Wade_ was overturned four years ago, I sent the email below.

I was outraged then. And today, I'm sickened by the damage anti-choice Republicans have inflicted on women and families in the years since.

_Within two years of the _Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization_ decision, 21 states had passed abortion bans_ — a devastating reminder that Republicans don't care in the least about women's safety, our freedom, or our most fundamental rights. Today, that number is even higher.

And abortion bans were just the beginning. Since _Roe_ fell, anti-choice Republicans have gone after access to mifepristone — a safe and effective medication used for abortion and miscarriage management — along with birth control and in vitro fertilization (IVF). These attacks remain in full throttle, and they have made clear that they will not stop unless we stop them.

So think about the damage they could do with two _more_ years in power.

clean_body: Think of the damage Republicans can do with two more years | It's time to fight. = Peter, when Roe v. Wade was overturned four years ago, I sent the email below. I was outraged then. And today, I'm sickened by the damage anti-choice Republicans have inflicted on women and families in the years since. Within two years of the Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization decision, 21 states had passed abortion bans — a devastating reminder that Republicans don't care in the least about women's safety, our freedom, or our most fundamental rights. Today, that number is even higher. And abortion bans were just the beginning. Since Roe fell, anti-choice Republicans have gone after access to mifepristone — a safe and effective medication used for abortion and miscarriage management — along with birth control and in vitro fertilization (IVF). These attacks remain in full throttle, and they have made clear that they will not stop unless we stop them. So think about the damage they could do with two more years in power. As you revisit my message from 2022, I hope you remember how you felt that day — the anger, the heartbreak, and the determination to fight back. Then, if you are able, please donate to our one-day match opportunity to help elect Democratic pro-choice women fighting for our reproductive freedoms from coast to coast. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thanks for standing with EMILYs List, Ellen R. Malcolm Founder and Chair Emerita, EMILYs List \----------Original Message--------- From: Ellen R. Malcolm, EMILYs List Sent: Sun., June 26, 2022 = Dear Peter, After almost 50 years as the law of the land, Roe v. Wade has been struck down and our constitutional right to freedom over our own bodies eliminated. I'm furious, Peter. Are you furious? If so: it's time to fight. The consequences for millions of our fellow Americans and countless families are coming fast or are already here. Reproductive care and essential health care services across the country are stopping. And the Republican Party is congratulating itself on a job well done — and preparing to go much further to rip away our rights. EMILYs List knows how to fight back, and we ARE fighting back, with every proud Democratic pro-choice woman we help elect in 2022. We have to channel our fury into action. We have to act together, and we have to act right now. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = We have 135 days, Peter. In 135 days, the fate of our hard-earned Democratic majorities in Congress, three dozen governorships, and thousands of powerful state and local offices will be decided at the ballot box. If Republicans prevail, the repercussions will be dire. You can be sure a national abortion ban will emerge in Congress. And Republicans could easily come after more of our inalienable rights as women, citizens, and equal participants in American society — like contraception, or marriage equality. Here's the silver lining: We've already endorsed 170 exceptional women for office who are unflinching fighters for choice and for families. These women have exactly what it takes to win some of the toughest races in the country and defy history in the moment we need it most. I know Democratic pro-choice women can do this because we've done it before. After the election of Donald Trump and the Me Too movement in 2018, we fought back and took control of the House and Senate. We have to protect those gains in 2022, and elect pro-choice majorities in the states. I believe in these fierce candidates. And I believe in this community more than ever. We won't stand for these attacks on our freedom, and we must elect Democratic pro-choice champions to every level of office who will never, ever give in to the forces who seek to control us and our destinies. We MUST fight back, and we have to do it now. There is so much that this little girl couldn't have imagined. One of the biggest? That she'd become one of the first women to represent Nevada in the U.S. Senate.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1bb81520-1107-4c09-8db6-d8414348fda7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But she also never could have imagined that when she was all grown up, she would be fighting to stop Republican extremists from taking away our most fundamental rights.
**It 's been four years since the Supreme Court overturned **_**Roe v. Wade**_**, ending our constitutional right to abortion - and with it, our right to make extremely personal decisions about our bodies, our health care, and our own families.**
Ever since, we've witnessed a relentless effort from the Trump administration and extremists in states across the country to restrict access to reproductive care - putting the lives of millions of women at risk in the process.
It breaks my heart to know that future generations will be growing up with fewer rights than the generations that came before. That's why I'm fighting back every day to protect and restore reproductive freedom nationwide.
I helped introduce the Right to Contraception Act in the Senate to protect the right to birth control - and the Let Doctors Provide Reproductive Health Care Act to protect the right of medical professionals to provide reproductive care. And on this day last year, I helped introduce the Women's Health Protection Act to restore the protections of _Roe v. Wade_.
Today and always, my promise to you is this: **I will never let up in the fight to ensure women have the freedom they deserve to make their own health care decisions without interference from politicians.** I am filled with gratitude to know that dedicated supporters like you are by my side.
* * *
##### `A personal note from Sen. Jacky Rosen:`
##### `My work in the Senate has always been defined by who I am and where I come from. Growing up as the granddaughter of immigrants and the daughter of a World War II veteran, my family instilled in me the values of hard work, determination, and persistence at a young age.`
##### `Now, I'm proud to fight tirelessly in the Senate to deliver progress for hardworking families like mine in Nevada and across our country. But with Donald Trump in the White House and Republicans in control of both houses of Congress, I need your grassroots support to keep up the fights that matter most.`
##### `Senate Democrats like me are the only thing standing in the way of Trump's extreme agenda that will hurt everyday Americans. That's why I need people like you on my side to help defend our progress and reclaim power from the GOP.`
##### `If you're with me, will you chip in now to help Democrats take back the Senate majority?`

We just got some tough news.
Inside Elections just moved our race from "Tilt Democratic" to "Toss-up."
That means one thing: This race is going to be one of the closest House races in the entire country.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
National Republicans have had their eye on this seat for years because they think it's one of their best opportunities to flip a district that will determine who controls Congress.
And now, one of the top election analysts in the country is confirming what we've known all along: This race will come down to the wire.
The truth is, I've never taken anything for granted. Not in 2022. Not in 2024. And certainly not now.
We won’t win automatically — not in a district this competitive. And to be honest, I wouldn’t want to. I work every day to earn this district’s votes because that’s exactly how democracy should work.
But now, we’re facing a flood of outside money that's about to pour into Southwest Washington because control of the House could come down to just a handful of seats.
That's why I'm asking for your help today.
If we're going to defend this seat, it's going to take all of us pulling together. Every volunteer shift matters. Every conversation matters. And yes, every donation matters too. Can you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can afford today to help us keep WA-03 blue? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]

To all public broadcasters,

Thank you. Thank you for enriching our lives — in rural and urban areas, and everywhere in between — with your various news and educational programs.

I couldn’t be more THRILLED to see Trump’s disgusting executive order blocked in court.

**But until your funding is resumed, I won’t stop fighting. I also know that his attempts to SILENCE the free press won’t end here.**

# [Cerebras gets absolutely gutted as the CEO admits the ugly truth:
Data center shortage is strangling AI](https://substack.com/redirect/7ca4fb41-fc4e-4269-a0fa-f63d3ad06fee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This morning's bloodbath is pure poetry. Cerebras just dropped its first public earnings since that monster $5.5 billion IPO in May: Q1 revenue exploded 94% to $193.4 million, full-year 2026 guidance $855-865 million, both smoking Wall Street. Net loss a measly $14 million instead of the expected $58.6 million. On paper? A beat. In reality? The stock got torched 15-17%, cratering below $200 to fresh post-IPO lows after debuting at $311 and pricing at $185. Why? Because the "misunderstood" margin forecast just body-slammed the bulls.
They're guiding core gross margins down to 38-41% for the year from 47% in Q1, a 10-15 point haircut because (drumroll please) they're forced to rent their own systems back from a big client and aggressively build their own damn data centers. CEO Andrew Feldman on CNBC this morning, straight face: "It's a grand irony that after all this technology... buildings are the limiting factor." Translation: we invented the rocket ship but there's nowhere to launch it.

Me? I'm short the dream, long the infrastructure choke points. This isn't a dip, it's the first real warning shot that the AI party is running out of venues. Pack your bags accordingly, or get left holding the empty server racks.

Partners Group gated its $8.6 billion vehicle at 10%, Cliffwater's $31 billion fund saw 17% asks, BlackRock 13%. Every major name is now telling LPs "sorry, your money's locked." This isn't isolated, it's systemic. Private credit was sold as liquid, diversified, safe yield. Turns out it's illiquid garbage when the music stops. Consumers buried in debt, bonds calling bullshit, Fed trapped and now the shadow banking shadow is cracking.

* **Losers?** Pension funds, insurers, retail proxies chasing 8% yield who now can't exit.
* **Next?** More gates, more markdowns, forced liquidations that bleed into public credit and equities.

This is 2008's cousin wearing a suit. I'm short the whole illiquidity complex and long volatility that's been asleep too long. The panic is real, ignore it and get destroyed.

Private credit backers (insurers are toast)](https://substack.com/redirect/7ca4fb41-fc4e-4269-a0fa-f63d3ad06fee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is the trade you dream about. Lee Robinson, the guy who scored 900% in the GFC betting against subprime, is back, shorting insurers like Lincoln National, MetLife, even Berkshire through CDS because they're stuffed with private credit.
He sees the exact same calm-before-Lehman vibe: low vol, low spreads, everyone pretending the $1.8 trillion untested debt market is fine. Parallels to software borrowers getting AI'd into bankruptcy, liquidity drying up. New fund, own capital in.
* **Winners?** Robinson and anyone smart enough to follow the second-order short.
* **Losers?** Insurers holding the bag when private credit marks down and writedowns hit earnings.
* **Next?** One big corporate blowup and the CDS blow out, insurers get repriced like 2008 banks.

I'm piling in right behind him. This is how legends print, spotting the calm that hides the storm. The 2008 playbook just got reloaded. Don't sleep on it or you'll be the one explaining losses to your boss.

# [Reddit degenerates and a new CFO ride to Wendy's rescue as burger flippers just became a squeeze play](https://substack.com/redirect/7ca4fb41-fc4e-4269-a0fa-f63d3ad06fee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Wendy's WEN, 31.8% shorted with 4.7 days to cover, rockets 22% in a week after tapping Potbelly's old CFO Steve Cirulis as chief strategy guy under new CEO Robert Wright. "Project Fresh" my ass! It's Project Short Squeeze.
Reddit's WallStreetBets lit the fuse on the beaten-down burger chain that had dropped 25%. Cirulis helped Wright turn Potbelly into a 500% stock rocket once; now they're repeating the script at Wendy's. Retail smelled blood, piled in, shorts got torched. Classic meme revival.
* **Winners?** The Reddit army that front-ran the turnaround narrative and the new management cashing the volatility pop.
* **Losers?** The hedge funds who stayed short a name with activist energy and fresh blood.
* **Next?** Watch if Wright starts issuing shares to milk the retail piggy bank, it's a classic move. Or if this fades into another dead-cat bounce before the real earnings test.

I'm not buying the fries, but I'm trading the volatility long gamma, short the bagholders who FOMO in at the top. Fast food just reminded everyone: never underestimate a heavily shorted name with a story and a mob.

# [Defense darling just learned politicians still run the show, Rheinmetall gets absolutely crushed 17% after Germany axes the warship contract](https://substack.com/redirect/7ca4fb41-fc4e-4269-a0fa-f63d3ad06fee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Defense stocks aren't immune to stupidity. Rheinmetall plunges 17%, biggest drop in over a year, after Berlin scraps the multi-billion F126 frigate program citing delays, cost overruns, and contractor risk. They're flipping to TKMS for eight MEKO-200s instead; TKMS stock jumps 10%. Analysts call it a surprise, Rheinmetall was confident pre-summer. Citi sees €115 downside risk to targets, questions naval ramp to €5bn by 2030. Morgan Stanley says limited 2030 hit since deliveries were 2031 anyway, but sentiment takes the beating.
* **Winners?** TKMS and anyone betting on German procurement chaos favoring the incumbent.
* **Losers?** Rheinmetall shareholders who bought the rearm-Europe narrative without reading the small print on politics.
* **Next?** More procurement whiplash across Europe, defense budgets loud but execution sloppy.

I'm using the dip to add selective names with actual contracts in hand and shorting the ones relying on promises. Governments sign checks, then change minds. Classic. Never forget who really pays.

The retail bagholders who bought the AI hype at 100x sales, the analysts who raised targets anyway like good little soldiers, and every CEO pretending buildings grow on trees. Next move? More pain this week as insiders dump. Then the market will either wake up and rerate the entire sector for reality... or keep pretending until the next earnings confession. Me? I'm short the dream, long the infrastructure choke points. This isn't a dip, it's the first real warning shot that the AI party is running out of venues. Pack your bags accordingly, or get left holding the empty server racks. | | | | ---|---|--- | November 15, 2025 | The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! The quiet collapse just screamed. Apollo slapped a 5% quarterly cap on its $25 billion Debt Solutions fund after 16.8% redemption requests. Partners Group gated its $8.6 billion vehicle at 10%, Cliffwater's $31 billion fund saw 17% asks, BlackRock 13%. Every major name is now telling LPs "sorry, your money's locked." This isn't isolated, it's systemic. Private credit was sold as liquid, diversified, safe yield. Turns out it's illiquid garbage when the music stops. Consumers buried in debt, bonds calling bullshit, Fed trapped and now the shadow banking shadow is cracking. Winners? The smart money who never drank the private credit Kool-Aid and anyone positioned for forced sales. Losers? Pension funds, insurers, retail proxies chasing 8% yield who now can't exit. Next? More gates, more markdowns, forced liquidations that bleed into public credit and equities. This is 2008's cousin wearing a suit. I'm short the whole illiquidity complex and long volatility that's been asleep too long. The panic is real, ignore it and get destroyed. Read and and don't say I didn't warn you when funds start popping like tins of dog food hit by a .357 Magnum. Support The Capitalist by getting the SubStack App This one's brutal. Citadel Securities drops the hammer: "Welcome to the politics of AI, the frontier is not for everyone." Translation? Open-market AI gold rush is over. Only a handful of players, backed by the right governments, the right capital, the right clearances, get the real models. Everyone else gets the scraps. Ken Griffin's shop just said out loud what we've known: AI supremacy is now national security policy, industrial policy, and straight geopolitics. Winners? The mega-fortress hyperscalers and defense-tied chip plays with Washington on speed dial. Losers? Every startup, every mid-tier, every nation-state without the muscle. The retail AI meme crowd is about to learn they were never invited to the real table. Next? Massive bifurcation, frontier stocks gap higher on government contracts while the rest get regulated or starved. I'm long the anointed few and short the pretenders. This isn't tech anymore; it's power. Adapt or get regulated into oblivion. Seconds out! Citadel just rang the bell! This is the trade you dream about. Lee Robinson, the guy who scored 900% in the GFC betting against subprime, is back, shorting insurers like Lincoln National, MetLife, even Berkshire through CDS because they're stuffed with private credit. He sees the exact same calm-before-Lehman vibe: low vol, low spreads, everyone pretending the $1.8 trillion untested debt market is fine. Parallels to software borrowers getting AI'd into bankruptcy, liquidity drying up. New fund, own capital in. Winners? Robinson and anyone smart enough to follow the second-order short. Losers? Insurers holding the bag when private credit marks down and writedowns hit earnings. Next? One big corporate blowup and the CDS blow out, insurers get repriced like 2008 banks. I'm piling in right behind him. This is how legends print, spotting the calm that hides the storm. The 2008 playbook just got reloaded. Don't sleep on it or you'll be the one explaining losses to your boss. Wendy's WEN, 31.8% shorted with 4.7 days to cover, rockets 22% in a week after tapping Potbelly's old CFO Steve Cirulis as chief strategy guy under new CEO Robert Wright. "Project Fresh" my ass! It's Project Short Squeeze. Reddit's WallStreetBets lit the fuse on the beaten-down burger chain that had dropped 25%. Cirulis helped Wright turn Potbelly into a 500% stock rocket once; now they're repeating the script at Wendy's. Retail smelled blood, piled in, shorts got torched. Classic meme revival. Winners? The Reddit army that front-ran the turnaround narrative and the new management cashing the volatility pop. Losers? The hedge funds who stayed short a name with activist energy and fresh blood. Next? Watch if Wright starts issuing shares to milk the retail piggy bank, it's a classic move. Or if this fades into another dead-cat bounce before the real earnings test. I'm not buying the fries, but I'm trading the volatility long gamma, short the bagholders who FOMO in at the top. Rheinmetall plunges 17%, biggest drop in over a year, after Berlin scraps the multi-billion F126 frigate program citing delays, cost overruns, and contractor risk. body:
The fight for democracy is the fight of our generation.
| | |
---
Hi there, it's Marc Elias.
For years, I've gone to court to stop Trump and defend democracy. Now, I'm working every day to safeguard voting rights, uphold the rule of law, and protect your freedom.
But I won't lie: **Trump and Senate Republicans' actions are actively putting all of that at risk – and it's going to take ALL of us to stop their destruction. And right now, that means helping leaders like Sherrod Brown win so we can restore a Democratic Senate majority.**
**[Grassroots supporters like you power our fight to flip the Senate so we can put a stop to the GOP's extremism and harmful policies. Will you split $5 between Sherrod Brown's campaign and the DSCC to help us stop Trump's enablers and flip the Senate blue?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133956479/629632175/-1453481972?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5158-bu-ndva&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMzIyODQ2Yi0yNzcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rNysPbll-EJUq7QtsfEeuCHLjZDOqlhmcHAt231OCvQ=)**
I'll explain:
Donald Trump is ignoring due process and openly mocking the courts. He's threatening the very foundation of our democracy by attacking fair, free, and secure elections. And he and his Republican friends are going after voting rights – _the very bedrock of our democracy._
But the DSCC and I are fighting back: As soon as Trump signed an executive order to interfere in our elections and threaten voting rights, we filed suit against him on behalf of Democrats nationwide. And the good news is, we've already notched some key victories in the case!
The fight isn't over yet. Donald Trump is an aspiring dictator – not just for a single day – and dictators never willingly give up power. We have to take it from them. And that's where all of us have the chance to make a difference.
